methods.label: Test the longest side
methods.explanation:
For a triangle whose longest side is \(c\), the Pythagorean theorem and its converse say that it is right exactly when the other two sides satisfy \(a^2+b^2=c^2\). Testing each triangle gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{I}:\quad&3^2+4^2=25=5^2,\\
\mathrm{II}:\quad&4^2+7.5^2=72.25=8.5^2,\\
\mathrm{III}:\quad&7^2+24^2=625=25^2,\\
\mathrm{IV}:\quad&3.5^2+4.5^2=32.5\ne30.25=5.5^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus exactly triangles \(\mathrm{I}\), \(\mathrm{II}\), and \(\mathrm{III}\) are right triangles, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Checking squared side lengths requires only elementary arithmetic and the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.
